title: Feature flag runbook rehearsal: UI + Rollouts + Analytics
content:
Purpose: rehearse the runbook for a feature-flagged UI rollout that touches the Rollouts dashboard, analytics ingestion, and the client-side SDK. Make sure owners, rollback triggers, and observability hooks are exercised before next-week canary.

Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Luis Fernandez (frontend), Maya Patel (backend/ingest), Samir Gupta (telemetry), Janelle Roberts (PM), + UX observer (Adrian).

Summary of scenario exercised:
- Target: enable `ff-new-route-inspector` for 2% of traffic for 48h. The change requires: console UI toggle, server-side flag gate in routing service, and a small telemetry event addition (route_inspector.opened).
- Goal: validate that UI toggle, rollout policy, and analytics produce clear signals for safe expansion or immediate rollback.

What we ran through (chronological):
1) Preflight checklist (Avery) - confirmed all green before flip:
   - Feature flag created in LaunchDarkly with matching key and proper tags. (checked)
   - Configured rollout policy: 2% initial, exponential ramp to 20% over 5 days if no regression. (checked)
   - Added runbook steps for manual abort + automatic rollback triggers (pager thresholds). (checked)
   - Staging smoke: UI toggle visible and route inspector renders with mock data. (checked)

2) Flip UI toggle in console (Luis) - immediate observations:
   - UI: toggle state updates across sessions within ~400ms. Minor CSS flash observed in Safari (low severity).
   - Instrumentation: new telemetry event `route_inspector.opened` emitted with properties {user_id_hash, route_id, flag_variant}. Events arrive in ingest within ~12s.

3) Backend gating (Maya) - server rollout verified:
   - Requests to /route/inspect return the new metadata only when flag enabled. Response tail latency unchanged (+7ms p95).
   - Added a defensive header X-FF-Rollout: variant to help tracing.

4) Telemetry and dashboards (Samir) - analytics validation:
   - Confirmed event schema in pipeline — missing field `route_owner` in 1% of events (data quality). Created INF-3126 to backfill and guard.
   - Rollup dashboard (Rollouts->Canary overview) updated to show feature-specific metrics: adoption rate, error-rate delta, latency delta, and UX retention.

Decisions made during rehearsal:
- If error-rate delta > 1.5% absolute within first hour, trigger automatic rollback. (Decision: enforce)
- If p95 latency increases by > 30ms and coincides with error spike, run emergency rollback and start postmortem.
- Cosmetic Safari flash: track as technical debt, do NOT block rollout. Prioritize for sprint-after-next.

Observed issues and action items:
- Missing `route_owner` in telemetry (Maya -> INF-3126) - severity: medium - ETA: 2026-05-18.
- Ingest latency spikes when traffic scaled in test harness from 200 -> 2k rps (Samir) - root cause: temporary backfill map overload in the transformer stage. Action: add buffered consumer and retry logic. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-05-20.
- CSS flash in Safari (Luis) - small visual jank when toggle applied; patch PR drafted (#2487). Owner: Luis. ETA: 2026-05-14.
- Runbook clarity: add explicit Slack escape hatch step (who to DM and exact message format). Owner: Avery. ETA: 2026-05-13 (updated).

Metrics to watch during live canary (2% initial):
- Adoption: fraction of eligible users seeing new route inspector. Target: 1.8% - 2.2%.
- Error-rate delta: compare 5m window vs baseline. Action threshold 1.5% absolute.
- p95 latency (route service) - threshold +30ms.
- Telemetry ingestion lag - target < 20s 95th.
- UX retention: users who open inspector and complete follow-up flow (if below baseline by >5% pause rollout).

Rollback cookbook (quick):
1) Flip LaunchDarkly flag to off.
2) Disable client-side toggle via Console (Avery) so no new sessions get experiment.
3) If traffic needs immediate reduction, route traffic away from canary region via smart-routing policy (SRE assistance).
4) Post-rollback: capture full diagnostics (trace ID list, ingest payload samples). Create postmortem ticket.

Communication plan during rollout:
- T+0: Slack announcement to #rollouts and #oncall with links to dashboards.
- T+30m: check-in message with snapshot: adoption, p95, errors.
- If auto-rollback triggers, incident message template (added to runbook).

Follow-ups and owners (short):
- Avery: update runbook with explicit Slack escape hatch and link to INF-3126. (ETA 2026-05-13)
- Maya: patch telemetry to include `route_owner` and add schema guard. (INF-3126, ETA 2026-05-18)
- Samir: stabilize ingest transformer (buffer/ retry), add alert for ingest lag > 20s p95. (ETA 2026-05-20)
- Luis: land small CSS patch and validate Safari fix in canary cohort. (PR #2487, ETA 2026-05-14)
- Janelle: coordinate UX observer run for first 24h and collect qualitative feedback.

Notes and questions for next rehearsal:
- Validate multi-region canary where rollout splits by region instead of global percentage.
- Exercise emergency rollback where A/B test has incompatible schema change in analytics (simulate missing fields).
- Confirm that rollback telemetry annotations are visible in traces and that console shows a clear status badge for aborted rollouts.

Appendix (quick references):
- Jira: INF-3124 (main rollout ticket), INF-3126 (telemetry fix).
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2487 (UI patch).
- Confluence: Feature Flag Runbook (link above).

Meeting length: 50m. Tone: practical, rehearsal-focused. Next rehearsal scheduled if any of the follow-ups miss ETA or before expanding to 10% cohort.

End of notes.
